about: Carrying a series' zone change to one of its copies (cal_core::zone_carry, DESIGN-series-time-zone.md section 23b and stage 13; decisions 143a to 146a, 120a). Each question is the series before and after its whole-series save (rule, start, zone; null for UTC), the start the applied zone answers left (appliedStart) and how far they moved its occurrences in wall minutes (movedMinutes, summed), the saved length where the end changed (newLengthMs, else null), one copy as its calendar stores it, the zones that calendar stores (timeZones: all, none or a list), whether it stores a series' end as a date (endsByDate) and today. The copy is paired with the series by instants: its occurrence nearest the series' first, less than 12 hours away, both patterns reaching past their starts and ends; it then moves by one wall shift, that occurrence read on the series' old clock plus the series' own shift, minus it read on the copy's clock (shiftMinutes). Failing that, a copy within 12 hours of the series' first new occurrence keeps its instants; else it is off the series' days. It keeps its own clock where that is the series' new one (both UTC, one canonical zone, or the same rules from today on); there, with no shift and its length right, it is unchanged. A shift equal to the copy's own as-the-rule-says or as-they-fall-now gives exactly that answer; any other moves it as a whole. zoneDays is how many days its first occurrence moves for the zone, read on the new clock before and after, a date move after the choice left out (negative is earlier). Refusals: not_a_series, all_day, zone_not_storable, off_pattern, rule_cannot_move with the rule's own reason; row facts first. Written by hand from tzdata's rules; the core, the phone's door and the desktop's WebAssembly door read this file.

rows.name: a-true-copy-as-they-fall-now
rows.note: The series that lost its Berlin zone (Mondays 23:30 UTC from Sunday 1 November), Berlin chosen as they fall now. A copy that is the same series gets the series' own answer: Tuesdays, the start kept, 60 minutes. Its occurrences keep their instants, so they read on the same day in Berlin before and after: zoneDays 0 (hole 0).

rows.name: a-true-copy-as-the-rule-says
rows.note: The same series, Berlin chosen as the rule says (-1380 minutes). The copy gets the series' own answer: Mondays, the start kept. Its first occurrence, Monday 2 November 23:30 UTC, reads Tuesday 00:30 in Berlin and moves to Monday 00:30: one day earlier on the new clock, zoneDays -1 (vor, hole 0).

rows.name: a-copy-in-the-other-half-year-comes-to-the-series-hour
rows.note: 144a: the series is Mondays 08:00 UTC from January, to Berlin as they fall now (09:00 Berlin, 60 minutes). A copy from June, Mondays 08:00 UTC, pairs with the series' first occurrence (4 January 08:00 UTC, its own pattern reaching back) and moves by the same 60 minutes of wall time: 09:00 Berlin, which in June is 07:00 UTC. Its own as-they-fall-now would have been 120 minutes (10:00 Berlin).

rows.name: copy-in-june-anchor-in-january-as-they-fall-now
rows.note: 144a near midnight: the series Mondays 22:30 UTC from January goes to Monday 23:30 Berlin (60 minutes). A June copy at the same UTC time comes to Monday 23:30 Berlin too, MO kept. Its first occurrence read Tuesday 00:30 in Berlin before (summer time) and Monday 23:30 after: zoneDays -1 (hole 0, the 144a midnight case).

rows.name: copy-in-january-anchor-in-june-as-the-rule-says
rows.note: The other way: the series Mondays 22:30 UTC from June goes to Berlin as the rule says, Monday 00:30 (-1320 minutes, the start moved back to Sunday 22:30 UTC). A January copy moves by the same -1320 minutes: Monday 22:30 UTC becomes Monday 00:30 Berlin, MO kept. In Berlin its first occurrence read Monday 23:30 before and Monday 00:30 after: the same day.

rows.name: copy-in-january-anchor-in-june-as-they-fall-now
rows.note: The same series as they fall now: Tuesday 00:30 Berlin (120 minutes). The January copy moves by 120 minutes of wall time: Monday 22:30 becomes Tuesday 00:30 Berlin, so its rule names Tuesday. In Berlin its first occurrence read Monday 23:30 before and Tuesday 00:30 after: one day later (zurueck).

rows.name: a-copy-an-hour-later-keeps-its-distance
rows.note: 145a: the series Mondays 09:00 UTC from January goes to 10:00 Berlin. A June copy at 10:00 UTC pairs with the series' first occurrence an hour away and keeps that hour: 11:00 Berlin (09:00 UTC in June), not the series' 10:00.

rows.name: a-copy-already-repaired-is-unchanged
rows.note: The lost-zone repair as the rule says, with a copy that already repeats Mondays 00:30 on Berlin. It is a day from the series' old occurrences, so the first pairing finds nothing; it stands on the series' first new occurrence, so it keeps its instants, and on its own clock with no move it is not written.

rows.name: a-copy-already-repaired-gets-a-new-end
rows.note: Hole 1: the same, with the end changed after the zone choice (90 minutes long). The copy stands right but its length does not: it is written with its own rule, start and exceptions, the new end, no shift and no day move.

rows.name: a-copy-on-berlin-at-the-old-instants-moves-a-day-earlier
rows.note: The lost-zone repair as the rule says, with a copy on Berlin at the series' old instants (Tuesdays 00:30 Berlin). It follows the series a day earlier: Mondays 00:30 Berlin, -1440 minutes, zoneDays -1.

rows.name: a-copy-on-berlin-from-june-pairs-by-instants
rows.note: The same repair with a Berlin copy that starts in June, Tuesdays 00:30 Berlin (Monday 22:30 UTC in summer). It pairs with the series' first occurrence in November (Tuesday 00:30 Berlin, 23:30 UTC), not at its own start, so it moves by the same -1440 minutes: Mondays 00:30 Berlin. Read at its June start the clocks differ by two hours, not one, and it would land on Sunday 23:30.

rows.name: a-copy-in-vienna-keeps-vienna
rows.note: 120a: Vienna has Berlin's rules from today on, so a copy on Vienna at the series' new instants is on the series' new clock, keeps Vienna and is not written.

rows.name: to-utc-a-copy-on-etc-utc-is-unchanged
rows.note: A series moved from Berlin to UTC (as they fall now, -60). A copy on Etc/UTC at the new instants is on the same clock (every UTC name is UTC) and is not written.

rows.name: to-utc-a-copy-on-berlin-is-written-without-a-zone
rows.note: The same change with a copy on Berlin: it gets the series' own answer and is written without a zone (tzid null for UTC).

rows.name: troll-on-a-calendar-that-cannot-store-it
rows.note: A series moved from UTC to Antarctica/Troll (+00 in January, so no move). The copy is on UTC, another clock, so it would take Troll; its calendar's list (an Exchange-style list without Troll) cannot store it.

rows.name: a-calendar-that-stores-no-zone
rows.note: The copy is a series in a calendar that stores no zone for a series (time_zones none).

rows.name: a-copy-without-a-rule
rows.note: A single event (or a device calendar's row): no series there, the zone does not apply.

rows.name: an-all-day-copy
rows.note: An all-day series has no zone of its own (46a).

rows.name: a-copy-whose-rule-cannot-be-read
rows.note: A rule no reader agrees on cannot move.

rows.name: every-other-week-in-the-other-parity
rows.note: The series repeats every other Monday from 4 January, the copy every other Monday from 11 January: no copy occurrence within 12 hours of the series' first, old or new.

rows.name: a-move-into-the-spring-gap
rows.note: The series Sundays 01:30 UTC from 1 November 2026 goes to 02:30 Berlin (60 minutes). A copy from 28 March 2027 moves by the same 60 minutes of wall time: 02:30 Berlin on the day the clocks skip it.

rows.name: a-rule-with-its-own-hour
rows.note: A copy whose rule names its own hour (BYHOUR) cannot move to another time of day.

rows.name: a-whole-move-with-a-deletion-and-an-end
rows.note: A June copy of the January series moves by 60 minutes as a whole, neither of its own answers: its deletion of 21 June moves with its occurrence (09:00 Berlin, 07:00 UTC), and its end on 28 June becomes through 28 June on Berlin.

rows.name: across-midnight-with-an-end-on-the-last-occurrence
rows.note: Daily 19:00 New York to Berlin as they fall now (01:00 the next day, 360 minutes). A copy ending on its 10 November occurrence (11 November 00:00 UTC) ends a day later on the new clock, through 11 November. On Berlin the occurrences stand at 00:00 UTC, so 20261111T235959Z would be one second before the 12th and need the 105a guard; the end is written as the last instant of the 11th there (142a).

rows.name: across-midnight-with-a-guarded-end-by-date
rows.note: The same copy ending 20261110T235959Z in a calendar that stores its end as a date (140a): it was typed for 10 November, so it ends through the 11th on Berlin.

rows.name: across-midnight-with-a-guarded-end-as-a-cut
rows.note: The same end in a calendar that does not: 105a reads it as a cut before the 10 November occurrence, so it ends through 9 November there and through the 10th on Berlin.

rows.name: a-deletion-that-cancels-nothing-stays
rows.note: The lost-zone repair as the rule says on a true copy with two deletions: the one on Monday 9 November moves with its occurrence to Monday 00:30 Berlin; the one on a Wednesday cancels nothing and stays as written.

rows.name: zone-then-a-date-one-day-later
rows.note: The January series to Berlin as they fall now (09:00 Berlin), then moved a day later on the new clock: 25 hours of wall time in all. The June copy moves by them too, to Tuesday 09:00 Berlin. The day move counted for the zone leaves the date move out: zoneDays 0.

rows.name: zone-then-a-date-says-only-the-zone-days
rows.note: The lost-zone repair as the rule says (-1380), then a day later (Tuesday 00:30 Berlin): 60 minutes in all. The true copy takes the series' answer for the zone and the day as a drag, as the series did, and ends as the saved series, its start on the series' first Tuesday (review round 3). Its first occurrence moves a day earlier for the zone (-1380 alone), so zoneDays is -1; the date move is the user's own.

rows.name: zone-and-a-new-length
rows.note: The lost-zone choice as they fall now with the end changed (90 minutes long): the copy gets the new length after its own start.

rows.name: two-choices-summed
rows.note: Mondays 19:00 Berlin, to New York as they fall now (13:00, -360), then to Tokyo as they fall now (Tuesday 03:00, +840): 480 minutes in all. A true copy on Berlin moves by the sum, which is its own as-they-fall-now to Tokyo.

rows.name: an-hourly-copy
rows.note: An hourly copy pairs at its own start, with no day check: 60 minutes of wall time, its start 09:00 Berlin (07:00 UTC in June), its end an instant moved the same way.

rows.name: a-repaired-copy-takes-a-later-time
rows.note: The lost-zone repair as the rule says, then the time moved an hour later on the new clock. The copy already repeats Mondays 00:30 on Berlin, where the series stood once its answer was applied: it pairs after, keeps its instants and takes the hour alone (+60). The day move for the zone is none.

rows.name: a-repaired-weekday-copy-is-unchanged
rows.note: Monday to Friday 23:30 UTC repaired as the rule says (Monday to Friday 00:30 Berlin). A copy that already repeats so on Berlin stands near both patterns, since its days are neighbours; its whole week matches only the new one. Unchanged.

rows.name: a-daily-copy-already-there-is-unchanged
rows.note: The same repair; the copy repeats every day 00:30 on Berlin. Both patterns miss two of its days a week, it pairs at no distance either way, and the pairing that moves it less wins: it stays.

rows.name: a-utc-copy-at-the-new-instants-keeps-them
rows.note: The same repair; the copy repeats Sunday to Thursday 23:30 UTC, the series' new instants. It pairs after and goes to Berlin keeping its instants (+60), on the series' days there.

rows.name: a-true-weekday-copy-follows-the-series
rows.note: The same repair; the copy is the old series itself, Monday to Friday 23:30 UTC. Its week matches the old pattern, not the new one (Friday and Sunday differ): it ends identical to the series' own answer.

rows.name: a-true-copy-from-midweek-follows-the-series
rows.note: Monday to Saturday 23:30 UTC from a Tuesday, as the rule says to Berlin. The copy is the old series; its first occurrence also stands on the series' first new one, but its week matches only the old pattern. It ends identical to the series' answer.

rows.name: a-repaired-copy-from-midweek-is-unchanged
rows.note: The same series; the copy is the saved series on Berlin. Its week matches only the new pattern: unchanged.

rows.name: a-copy-equal-to-the-saved-series-across-autumn
rows.note: Mondays 23:30 UTC from a Saturday before Berlin's summer time ends, as they fall now (Tuesday 01:30 Berlin, +120 at the start). Every occurrence after the change stands an hour from the old pattern. A copy equal to the saved series pairs after at no distance and before only an hour off: unchanged.

rows.name: a-copy-equal-to-the-saved-series-across-spring
rows.note: The 14th, 00:30 Berlin before summer time, to UTC as they fall now (the 13th, 23:30). A copy equal to the saved series stands an hour from the old pattern in summer: unchanged.

rows.name: a-copy-equal-to-the-saved-series-from-the-fold
rows.note: Sundays 01:30 UTC from Berlin's second 02:30, to Berlin as they fall now. A copy equal to the saved series: unchanged.

rows.name: a-copy-on-a-day-of-the-year-is-off-pattern
rows.note: A weekly Monday series and a copy on the 100th day of each year: the reader cannot follow its days, so it pairs on none and is refused.

rows.name: a-copy-on-a-set-position-is-off-pattern
rows.note: A weekly Monday series and a copy on the last Friday of each month: refused, as above.

rows.name: a-copy-an-hour-after-keeps-it-across-a-change
rows.note: Mondays 00:00 UTC from a start before New York's autumn change, as they fall now (Sundays 20:00 New York). The series' first new occurrence stands an hour from its old one. A UTC copy an hour later is on the old clock: it follows the old series and keeps its hour (145a), Sundays 21:00 New York.

rows.name: a-copy-half-an-hour-after-keeps-it-across-a-change
rows.note: The same, with the copy half an hour later: Sundays 20:30 New York.

rows.name: a-copy-on-the-new-clock-near-the-series-stays
rows.note: The same series; the copy already repeats Sundays on New York, an hour before the old series' first occurrence and at the series' new one. On the new clock it already stands as the series does: unchanged.

rows.name: a-copy-at-the-applied-series-takes-a-day-earlier
rows.note: Monday to Friday 06:30 UTC to New York as they fall now, then a day earlier on the new clock. A copy that is the series as its answer left it takes the day alone (-1440) and lands on the saved series, Sunday to Thursday 01:30 New York, though New York's spring change lies in the week compared.

rows.name: every-other-week-re-anchored-is-refused
rows.note: Every other Monday 23:30 UTC, repaired to Berlin as the rule says. The series' own answer keeps its start, which reads a week later on Berlin, so its weeks flip (TODO). A copy from the other half-year moved by the answer would stand a week off the saved series: it is named instead of written.

rows.name: every-other-week-re-anchored-an-hour-later-is-refused
rows.note: The same series and a UTC copy an hour later: refused for the same reason.

rows.name: every-other-week-a-true-copy-ends-as-the-series
rows.note: The same series; the copy is the series as it stood. It takes the series' own answer and ends as the series.

rows.name: a-true-every-day-copy-takes-the-series-answer
rows.note: Every day 23:30 UTC with an end and a deletion, repaired to Berlin as the rule says. Both patterns hold every day; the copy is on the old clock and identical, so it follows the old series and ends as the series: the same deletion, the same end.

rows.name: a-copy-three-hours-later-across-spring
rows.note: Daily 00:30 Berlin from the night of the spring change, to UTC as they fall now (23:30 UTC). A Berlin copy at 03:30 summer time, first standing after the change, is on the old clock: it moves as the series' occurrences do, to 02:30 UTC.

rows.name: a-utc-copy-of-a-berlin-series-across-autumn
rows.note: Monday to Friday 18:00 Berlin from a week with the autumn change, to Tokyo as the rule says. A copy on UTC at the same instants follows the old series: Monday to Friday 01:00 Tokyo, a day earlier, as the series.

rows.name: a-copy-two-hours-later-across-autumn
rows.note: Mondays 23:30 UTC from a Saturday before Berlin's autumn change, as they fall now (Tuesdays 01:30 Berlin). A UTC copy two hours later keeps its two hours: Tuesdays 03:30 Berlin.

rows.name: a-true-copy-of-a-set-position-series
rows.note: The last Friday of each month 08:00 UTC to Berlin. The reader cannot follow such days, so the copy pairs at its own start: a true copy ends as the series.

rows.name: a-copy-at-the-applied-series-in-the-spring-gap
rows.note: Saturdays and Sundays 02:30 New York to Berlin, then an hour earlier. The saved series' first occurrence falls in Berlin's spring gap; the copy at the applied series takes the hour alone (-60), as from the gap's nominal time.

rows.name: a-true-yearly-copy-takes-the-series-answer
rows.note: Every March, 00:30 Berlin, to UTC as the rule says. A true copy ends as the series.

rows.name: a-true-weekday-copy-as-now-then-a-day-earlier
rows.note: Monday to Friday 23:30 UTC to Berlin as they fall now (+60), then a day earlier. In all the copy moves -1380, which is also its own as-the-rule-says; taken as one shift it kept its start and lost its first occurrence (review round 3). Composed as the series' was, zone answer then the day as a drag, it ends as the saved series.

rows.name: a-true-weekday-copy-to-new-york-then-a-day-later
rows.note: The same to New York (-300), then a day later: it ends as the saved series, with no occurrence left at its old instant.

rows.name: an-offset-weekday-copy-as-now-then-a-day-earlier
rows.note: The Berlin case with a copy half an hour earlier: it keeps its distance (145a), its start half an hour before the saved series'.

rows.name: every-other-week-a-true-copy-then-an-hour-later
rows.note: Every other Monday repaired to Berlin as the rule says, then an hour later. The true copy takes the series' answer and the hour as a drag, and ends as the saved series, weeks included.

rows.name: a-copy-from-the-other-half-year-then-an-hour-later
rows.note: Mondays 08:00 UTC from January to Berlin as they fall now (09:00 Berlin), then an hour later. A copy from June comes to the series' hour, 10:00 Berlin (144a).
